goals: mechanistic: quantify how elevation controls snowmelt-onset day-of-year across SNOTEL sites via the local temperature/precip-phase lapse rate
validation: assess ELM snowpack (SWE, melt-onset timing) skill against observed SNOTEL SWE at each station
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (acting through downscaled temperature & precip phase)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves snowpack energy/mass balance and can be validated against SNOTEL SWE; the elevation-as-climate driver, however, lives in the FORCING, which the stack does not vary with elevation.

answerable: ELM snowpack skill (modeled SWE, accumulation/ablation timing) validated against observed SNOTEL SWE at each of the 6 station locations, conditional on supplied forcing
melt-onset DOY as simulated at each site GIVEN its forcing

not_answerable.aspect: elevation control on snowmelt-onset DOY (the primary question)
not_answerable.why: no elevation-downscaling of forcing: temperature lapse rate, elevation-dependent precip and precip-phase are not applied, so columns at different elevations receive identical atmospheric drivers and cannot express an elevation-driven melt-onset gradient

not_answerable.aspect: resolving the local lapse rate between same-ridge stations
not_answerable.why: the lapse rate is a property of the forcing field, which is uniform across columns; the stack cannot derive or impose a station-to-station lapse rate
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled forcing with configurable/observation-constrained lapse rate

sampling_strategy.approach: observation-pinned (validation-driven), no exploratory elevation stratification until downscaled forcing exists

bands: one band per SNOTEL station elevation — realized only if downscaled forcing is added; otherwise nominal

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Under uniform forcing, intermediate-elevation exploratory columns would produce a spurious 'elevation' signal (soil, not climate). No exploratory columns are added until elevation-downscaled forcing makes the elevation axis physically meaningful.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Columns pinned to the 6 SNOTEL station locations, which by design span the elevation range and include same-ridge pairs (<12 km apart) needed for the lapse-rate question.

sampling_plan.reason: One ELM column co-located at each of the 6 SNOTEL SWE stations to validate modeled snowpack/melt-onset against observations; spans the elevation range and captures same-ridge station pairs.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — one ELM column per station compared to that station's daily SWE time series
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE, and melt-onset DOY error (date SWE begins sustained decline)

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled forcing (temperature lapse rate + elevation-dependent precip & precip-phase)
requires_capabilities.why: elevation controls melt onset through the atmospheric gradient, not the land surface; without it columns at different elevations see identical forcing
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire primary question — elevation control on melt-onset DOY and local lapse-rate resolution

requires_capabilities.why: melt-onset detection and SNOTEL comparison require exported daily SWE
day-of-year of onset must be extracted consistently from modeled and observed SWE series
requires_capabilities.blocks: quantifying the DOY metric the question asks for

requires_capabilities.why: map station coordinates and daily SWE records to columns for validation
credible seasonal snow energy balance needs equilibrated initial states

assumptions: SNOTEL station coordinates and elevations are resolvable downstream from the station metadata; not invented here.
The 6 stations collectively span the domain elevation range and include at least one same-ridge pair for the lapse-rate objective.
A representative forcing period within 1980-2018 will be selected downstream; melt-onset climatology needs multiple snow seasons.
open_questions: Can observation-constrained lapse rates be derived from the SNOTEL air-temperature records themselves to drive an elevation-downscaling capability?
Which specific stations form same-ridge pairs, and what is their elevation separation?
Is inter-annual variability in melt-onset (multi-year climatology) required, or a single representative water year?
